Local only. Plan: `.claude/plans/PLAN-v1-alpha-close-the-gap.md`. Open each session in `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto`, set model and effort, paste the prompt. Sessions run unattended; they come back to you only to merge.

| Session | Work | `/model` | `/effort` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 Release model | F1 -> F2 -> G -> H -> M | Opus 5.5 | medium |
| 2 Publish chain | D -> L -> J | Sonnet 5.5 | medium |
| 3 Fixes | A, B, C (workflow), then K (after G merges) and N | Sonnet 5.5 | medium |
| 5 Identity and graph | E -> I | Sonnet 5.5 | medium |
| 4 Evidence (after E and F2 merge) | Q | Sonnet 5.5 | medium |

Opus spend is limited to Session 1 (one cross-cutting semantic change, where a rework loop costs more than Opus) and to subagents: an Opus design note at the start of L, E and Q, and the Opus reviewer per PR.

Capacity: disk is the limit (about 98 GB free; stale worktree `target/` dirs hold about 89 GB, all regenerable). With debug info off, expect a few GB per active worktree. Sessions 1, 3 (three Wave 0 worktrees) and 5 build at once from the start; Session 2 starts with them because J's first change is tiny, and its heavier builds overlap Wave 0 finishing.

Before launch, free the stale build output (build artifacts only, no source or branches touched):

```
cd ~/Projects/callisto && rm -rf .claude/worktrees/*/target
```

Launch all from a shell in the repo (each prints an id; `claude agents` lists them, `claude attach <id>` watches one):

```
cd ~/Projects/callisto
claude --bg --model opus   --effort medium "Run Session 1 in .claude/plans/LAUNCH-v1-alpha-sessions.md."
claude --bg --model sonnet --effort medium "Run Session 2 in .claude/plans/LAUNCH-v1-alpha-sessions.md."
claude --bg --model sonnet --effort medium "Use a workflow: run Session 3 in .claude/plans/LAUNCH-v1-alpha-sessions.md."
claude --bg --model sonnet --effort medium "Run Session 5 in .claude/plans/LAUNCH-v1-alpha-sessions.md."
# after E and F2 merge:
claude --bg --model sonnet --effort medium "Run Session 4 in .claude/plans/LAUNCH-v1-alpha-sessions.md."
```

## Session 1

```
Implement work packages F1, F2, G, H, then M from .claude/plans/PLAN-v1-alpha-close-the-gap.md, one PR each, in order. Its root-cause table (R1, R6) and settled decisions are the spec. Trail: "Managed prerelease and inferred release PRs" (create it if absent).
Done when: a pre cycle runs end to end through the release-PR flow (pre enter -> beta.0 -> fresh fix -> beta.1 -> nothing new -> no PR -> pre exit -> stable), inferred-only changes open a release PR, malformed-only changesets fail decide, and a Changesets v3 pre.json repo works mid-cycle.
Follow .claude/plans/LAUNCH-v1-alpha-sessions.md "Rules".
```

## Session 2

```
Implement work packages D, L, then J from .claude/plans/PLAN-v1-alpha-close-the-gap.md, one PR each, in order. Its root-cause table (R3, R7) and settled decisions are the spec. Trails: #357 for D; "Publish isolation and trusted publishing" for L and J (create it if absent).
Done when: generated workflows carry any valid branch name exactly in both templates; no job that runs project code holds id-token or registry credentials; npm-family publishes a packed tarball with --ignore-scripts; twine and crates.io can publish with no token through native OIDC (unproven against real registries until I run it).
Follow .claude/plans/LAUNCH-v1-alpha-sessions.md "Rules".
```

## Session 3

```
Use a workflow for work packages A, B and C from .claude/plans/PLAN-v1-alpha-close-the-gap.md: one worktree and PR each, pipeline implement (sonnet) -> mutants -> fresh review (opus) -> gate, under 10 agents, cargo lock shared. Trail #357.
Then K (after Session 1 merges G) and N.
Done when: policy recipes fail when cargo fails; the HTTP parser keeps a body with blank lines; JSON input errors carry their origin; a Changesets v2 or v3 config migrates with every ignored key reported; peer dependents get a patch by default.
Follow .claude/plans/LAUNCH-v1-alpha-sessions.md "Rules".
```

## Session 5

```
Implement work packages E, then I from .claude/plans/PLAN-v1-alpha-close-the-gap.md, one PR each. Its root-cause table (R2, R4) and settled decisions are the spec. Trail #357.
Done when: equivalent PyPI or crates.io names cannot both be admitted and two such owners produce zero provider effects; relative workspace: lookup is indexed, with before/after bench numbers.
Follow .claude/plans/LAUNCH-v1-alpha-sessions.md "Rules".
```

## Session 4 (after E and F2 merge)

```
Implement work package Q from .claude/plans/PLAN-v1-alpha-close-the-gap.md. Choose the narrowest test-only way past registry_endpoint.rs's https rule. Trail: "Release recovery evidence" (create it if absent).
Done when: `just verify-real` rehearses partial publish -> rerun adopts, delayed visibility, a conflicting tag and a missing Python artifact against local npm, cargo and PyPI registries through production registry binding, and exits nonzero on any wrong outcome.
Follow .claude/plans/LAUNCH-v1-alpha-sessions.md "Rules".
```

## Rules

- Before each WP: `git fetch`; re-verify the plan's finding against current main (other sessions merge in between). If another session already owns the WP's branch, skip to your next WP.
- Work in a named worktree per WP (EnterWorktree), branched off origin/main. No stacks. Each worktree builds into its own `target/`, so builds in different worktrees run in parallel with no lock; never run two builds in the same worktree.
- Build budget, exported once per session: `CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0` and `CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0` (debug info is most of each `target/`; dropping it cuts disk and link time), `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=$(( $(getconf _NPROCESSORS_ONLN) / 4 ))` and the same value for nextest `--test-threads`, so four builders share the CPU.
- Mutation testing runs in place in the WP worktree after committing: `cargo mutants --in-place --in-diff <diff>`; it reuses the worktree's `target/` instead of copying the tree.
- Start independent pieces early in their own worktrees: Session 1 runs G's `pre.json` reader/writer (`model/format/pre.rs`) as a subagent with `isolation: "worktree"` while it works on F1; Session 2 ships J's twine environment change (`runner.rs`) first. Only the parts that touch shared files wait for their chain.
- Start the reviewer subagent as soon as the diff is final, in parallel with the gate and mutation run; it reads, it never builds.
- When a WP's PR is open and green, `rm -rf <worktree>/target`; after merge, remove the worktree and its local branch.
- Fix the root cause by the first rung that works: type or private constructor, exhaustive match, existing lint, one test at the real boundary. Write that test first. Delete checks the type makes redundant. Fix siblings in the same PR.
- Specs, ADRs and docs/architecture change in the same PR as behaviour.
- Gate by exit code, unsandboxed in the worktree: `just pre-push && just lint && just doc-check && just test`, then `cargo mutants --in-diff` on the WP's Rust diff with zero missed (an equivalent mutant gets one line in the PR body).
- Design-heavy WPs (L, E, Q): first spawn one Opus subagent (general-purpose, model opus) with the plan's finding and root-cause row; it returns a short design (types, signatures, call sites to migrate, the boundary test). Implement against it yourself.
- One fresh-context reviewer per PR (general-purpose, model opus) given only the diff and the finding. Apply what holds up.
- Stay at the launched effort; do not escalate unless the same gate failure repeats.
- Ship without asking: signed commit, `callisto add` changeset for released-behaviour changes, push, `entire trail ci-pr`. No session links. Never merge.
- Ask me only when something requires me: a credential or account, or a plan claim that is false in a way that changes the design.

The decision records `consumed_changesets`, so E165 compares sets |
12:| R2 | Native identity is a raw `String`; normalization is free helpers some callers apply | F01 high: PEP 503-equivalent PyPI names admitted as two owners (`walk.rs:298`), one upload, both tags. Config rules, tags, `add` compare raw | `NativeName` in `callisto-model::identity`: private field, `new(Ecosystem, &str)`, keeps display spelling, `Eq/Hash/Ord` on the canonical key (PyPI PEP 503, Cargo lowercase with `_`->`-`, npm exact). `native_owner`, `IdentityIndex.native`, `ReleasePackageId.name`, config rule matching key on it |
13:| R3 | Values lose structure at boundaries: refs, YAML scalars, HTTP framing, input origin travel as `&str` | F04 `last_ref_segment` takes the last `/` (`init.rs:734`, two callers); F05 seven raw `replace()` into YAML (`init.rs:902-909`), `__COMMIT__` never parsed as `CommitSha`; F06 `rsplit_once("\r\n\r\n")` truncates a body with a blank line (`http.rs:56`; fails loudly); F10 every JSON parse error is E281/usage and paths ignore `--cwd` (`io.rs:19`); `checkpoint.rs` trailer search, `ls-tree` without `-z` | `BranchName` (only `from_full_ref` or `git check-ref-format --branch`); one `WorkflowScalar` encoder that `render_workflow` requires by type; header-first HTTP parse; `enum JsonInput { Stdin, Inline, File(PathBuf) }` through `resolve_file_arg` |
14:| R4 | One resolution, two implementations, no index | F07 O(E x P) relative `workspace:` lookup (`walk.rs:34-68,776`; 12x at 800 packages); `npm.rs:92-113` resolves the same path again and swallows errors | Canonical-dir -> `PackageId` index built once; both callers use it |
15:| R5 | Checks that cannot fail | F08 `! cargo tree | grep` passes when cargo fails (`justfile:99,111`); `coverage-per-crate` passes on empty data; bench prints "failed" and exits 0; flaky graph test is fixture portability (bsdtar `._*` with xattrs, bare `cargo` from PATH) | Boundaries move into `deny.toml`; `set shell := ["bash", "-euo", "pipefail", "-c"]`; bench exits 1; fixture uses `$CARGO` and `COPYFILE_DISABLE=1` |
16:| R6 | Wire compatibility assumed, not modeled | v3 `pre.json` (`{mode, tag}`) fails to parse (`pre.rs:106-133`); callisto writes v2 only, drops unknown keys; `.changeset/pre/` ignored and a move there fails E165 `UnexpectedPath`; ADR 1 says "same shape" | `enum PreStateShape { V2, V3 }` read from the file, written back in the shape read. Retained notes become `Source::RetainedChangeset` whichever shape stored them |
17:| R7 | Publish credentials and untrusted code share a process or job | Simple template: one `release` job builds and publishes with `id-token: write`; matrix `build` job runs project build code with `id-token: write` (for attestations); npm publish runs from the source directory, so lifecycle scripts run inside the process that holds npm's OIDC variables | Pack, then publish the tarball with `--ignore-scripts` in a job that runs no project code; attestation in its own job over uploaded artifacts; `id-token` only on that job and the publish job |

## How the swarm runs

- One named worktree per WP, branch off `main`, no stacks; merge in wave order.
- Builds: each worktree has its own target dir; every cargo invocation takes one machine-wide lock (`flock $TMPDIR/callisto-cargo.lock cargo ...`), so agents overlap on thinking and editing, never on builds.
- Per WP: the implementer writes the regression first, driving the real binary or function at the boundary named in the finding, then the type change, then deletes checks the type now covers.
- Proof by exit code: `just pre-push && just lint && just doc-check && just test`; `cargo mutants --in-diff` on the WP diff with zero missed except argued equivalents (it found two real gaps on a caliper branch today); sibling sweep listed in the PR body.
- Review: one fresh-context Opus reviewer per WP, given the diff and the finding, not the implementer's reasoning.
- Gates run unsandboxed in the worktree: sandboxed runs fail tests that write inside the repo and look like defects.
- Ship: signed commit, changeset via `callisto add`, push, link a trail (#357 for A-E, I; #250 or a new prerelease trail for F-H, K, M, N; a new publish-security trail for L, J).
- Orchestration: a Workflow script can run each wave as a pipeline (implement -> mutate -> review -> gate), with the build lock as the only shared resource; it needs an explicit "use a workflow".

Decided; sessions do not ask.

8. One changed-without-changeset flag on `status`.
9. Builds run in parallel across worktrees (each has its own `target/`); never two in one worktree. WP A rewords AGENTS.md's "Never run cargo builds in parallel" to say "in the same checkout".

**E.**
- **Behavior:** PEP 503-equivalent PyPI names and case/`-`/`_`-equivalent Cargo names now fail loading with E100. Selectors, `[[package]]` rules and history checks use the same equivalence.
- **Mutation testing:** 49 caught, 15 unviable and 1 missed. The missed mutant empties `Hash::hash` for `NativeName`. It is equivalent because an empty hash is still consistent with `Eq`. It needs one line in the PR body.
- **Force-push:** I amended and force-pushed #561 (`--force-with-lease`) to fold a lint fix into the tests commit.

**I.** At 800 pnpm packages with relative paths:

| Command | Before | After |

| `status` | 4.9 s | 0.6 s |
| `version --dry-run` | 7.6 s | 0.8 s |

- **Fixture and bench:** I added a pnpm-relative shape to the perf fixture and the bench.

**Open items**
- **Audit failure:** #561's audit fails on RUSTSEC-2026-0542. #560 fixes it in `deny.toml`, so I added no ignore.
- **Rebases:** after #560 and #561 merge, rebase #563 onto main. It conflicts with #560 in `crates/callisto-cli/benches/commands.rs`: keep both A's change and the pnpm shape, then re-run the gates.
- **Breaking?:** E's changeset is a `callisto-cli` patch with an **Action:** paragraph. Existing workspaces with such duplicate names will now fail to load, so decide whether it should be `**Breaking:**`.
- **Not covered:** glob patterns like `pypi/my-*` still match the manifest spelling, noted in E's changeset.
- **Cargo rule:** the plan's "Cargo `foo-bar`/`foo_bar` is E100" had no code behind it, so E introduces it (settled decision 4 in the plan).

18	## Commands
19	
20	- Full pipeline: `just ci` (includes the 90% coverage gate). `just test`, `just lint`, `just fmt`.
21	- Before every push or PR: `just pre-push && just lint && just doc-check && just test`, and `just ci` before marking a PR ready. Judge each by its exit code. Never tail or grep the output for success (a compile error prints no "failed" line), and never report a check as passed that was not run.
22	- Commits must be signed: the ruleset requires it. Never pass `-c commit.gpgsign=false`. After pushing, `gh api repos/orin-dx/callisto/commits/<sha> --jq .commit.verification.reason` must say `valid`.
23	- Performance: `just bench` times `status`, `version --dry-run` and `release --dry-run` over generated workspaces and counts the git processes each starts (`CALLISTO_BENCH_SHAPES=1` lists which). A change that adds a git process per package fails review.
24	- Scoped iteration: one `cargo test -p <crate>` or `cargo clippy -p <crate> --all-targets -- -D warnings` at a time.

content.text:
Both fixes are pushed, and GitHub reports `verification.reason: valid` for all three commits. I replied to nobody on the lead channel, so this is the report.

**#561 (WP E).** The callisto/169 finding is fixed and resolved on the trail (`entire trail finding resolve 01M7PDZH364D`).
- **Cause:** history ownership compared names with `NativeName`, so Cargo `foo_bar` was taken as owning npm `foo-bar`'s tag.
- **Fix:** historical ownership compares literal spellings again, as a default tag `foo-bar@` does. PyPI keeps its existing PEP 503 rule from before E.
- **Test:** the regression test fails before the fix and passes after.
- **Commits:** the fix is `d69bd794e`. I merged the owner's `c4fd037a0` into it as `23799cdff` and pushed without force. `git ls-remote` shows `23799cdff`.
- **Checks:** `just pre-push`, `just lint`, `just doc-check` and `just test` exited 0 on the merged state. I did not re-run mutation testing after this change.
- **Changeset:** unchanged, pending the owner's Breaking decision.

**#563 (WP I).** I merged main in and resolved the conflict in `crates/callisto-cli/benches/commands.rs`. It keeps A's `failed` flag and exit-1 behavior plus the pnpm-relative shape. The merge commit is `7f71226c4`. All four gates exited 0 and `git ls-remote` shows `7f71226c4`.

The new `names_equal` helper is back in `crates/callisto-graph/src/history.rs`. Cargo equivalence still applies to duplicate detection, selectors and `[[package]]` rules, but not to historical tag ownership.

The PyPI normalization on the same path is untouched. A PyPI `my_pkg` beside an npm `my-pkg` could hit the same kind of mix-up. I did not investigate it.

The PyPI sibling reproduced and is fixed on #561. The branch is pushed (`git ls-remote` shows `664170d00`) and GitHub reports `valid` for that commit's signature.

- **Reproduction:** with PyPI `foo_bar` beside npm `foo-bar`, then npm removed and the package renamed `foo-bar`, `may_have_held_name_at` returned true. PEP 503 normalization credited the npm tag to the PyPI package. The test failed for PyPI and passed for Cargo before the fix, and covers both ecosystems now.
- **Fix:** one literal-spelling comparison replaces `names_equal` for every ecosystem. A default tag `{name}@` carries the declared spelling, so equivalence never applied to tag ownership.
- **Cleanup:** the PyPI first-word search special case and the now-unused `ecosystem` parameter on `declares` are gone. I rewrote the two earlier history tests to the literal rule.
- **Mutation testing:** I ran `cargo mutants --in-place --in-diff` over `c4fd037a0..HEAD`, which covers `d69bd794e` plus the new commit. 14 mutants: 12 caught, 2 unviable, 0 missed. The earlier `Hash::hash` mutant is outside that diff and is still the one equivalent mutant to note in the PR body.
- **Checks:** `just pre-push`, `just lint`, `just doc-check` and `just test` exited 0 before the commit. The gate was not re-run after the commit. I did not run `just ci`.
- **Shas:**
  - **Fix commit:** `664170d00`.
  - **Earlier Cargo fix:** `d69bd794e`.
